analysis.title: GS TMT SPEC SALES: MSFT outage; Nvidia investor debate; Wise settles in Belgium; AMAT solid; Cisco beats; CTS Eventim mixed
key_insights: Microsoft 365 outage on Friday 13 Nov: Outlook, Teams and Copilot were degraded by an overwhelmed core process and an unexplained traffic surge. The desk says it was not a cyberattack, and MSFT was still down at the time of writing with users on backup email.

Jensen Huang's resignation as Nvidia CEO dominated trading, with Colette Kress named interim CEO. NVDA traded as much as -14.3% before closing -4.3%. QQQ finished modestly green after a -1.5% open, and semis recovered from an early -3.5%.
Relative winners on the Nvidia news were AMD (+6%), AVGO (+5.5%), ANET (+5%), CLS (+5% on TPU exposure) and GOOGL (+1.8%) as the main non-semi beneficiary on custom-chip share.

Neoclouds reversed the prior session's strength (NBIS -17%, CRWV -7%) on worries about losing Nvidia as the ecosystem's financing backstop. China-exposed names sold off on remote-control rules and possible Megaspeed/Singapore scrutiny (BABA -7%, VNET and GDS both about -11%).

The Nvidia debate is now structural. Nvidia has acted as lender of last resort to parts of the AI ecosystem, and its edge has leaned on Jensen's personal relationships: multi-year capacity pre-purchases, ties with Asian suppliers and credibility to underwrite long-duration demand. The open question is whether a new CEO has the same willingness or authority to deploy the balance sheet.

Physical supply is unlikely to be disrupted near term, but the durability of Nvidia's pre-commitment model is unclear. If the spying allegations gain traction, a return of the MATCH Act is a secondary risk, negative for ASML and to a lesser extent ASM.

Wise: results broadly in line with the Street, and the settlement removes the Belgium overhang with no admission of wrongdoing. The settlement amount was not disclosed, which the desk reads as immaterial. US licensing remediation is complete, with an update expected in 2027. The desk expects the stock to rise on the in-line numbers plus the removal of the overhang.

Wise detail: net revenue growth implies H2 deceleration to about 18% y/y ex-FX versus 22% in H1, at the upper end of FY27 guidance of 15-20%, which GIR sees as conservative. Gross margin was 84% in the quarter, opex pace has peaked, and Platform is about 6% of cross-border volume versus about 5% at FY26 results, with two top-20 US bank wins live in H1 FY27. GIR IBT estimates change by -1% to +3% across FY27-31E with revenue unchanged.

AMAT: solid quarter with revenue and margin guidance above expectations. The desk calls it a neutral read to semicap since most peers have already reported. Management set 2027 WFE growth of about 30%, in line with peers and constrained by cleanroom additions. GIR forecasts about 45%, implying upside to Street expectations, and GIR sees share gains as WFE growth accelerates in 2027.

Cisco: beat and raise on networking and opex, with a better-than-expected margin outlook and strong operating leverage. Product orders missed, up 21% y/y (+14% ex-webscale AI) versus +35% (+25% ex-webscale) in F4Q26. Campus orders rose about 15% y/y, decelerating for a third straight quarter, and hyperscale plus SP orders also slowed. Rising hyperscale mix may weigh on gross margin in F2H27.

CTS Eventim 3Q26 was mixed: revenue missed on weaker Live Entertainment while Ticketing was in line. Group adj. EBITDA was in line, with a 16.5% margin versus 16.1% consensus on better Ticketing margins. FY26 guidance was reiterated, and GIR changes 2026-31E group revenue by -1% and adj. EBITDA by 0% on average.

Nebius: Q3 beat, but FY26 revenue guidance was set at the lower end of $3.0-3.4B versus $3.4B consensus because third-party GPU capacity delays push supply into H1 2027. The desk says contracts are intact and demand unimpaired. The stock reversed from +5% to -9% pre-market on the guidance, with Nvidia exposure the other debate.

Nebius 2027 and funding: capex guidance of $40-45B is about 50% above the $28.8B consensus at the midpoint, with 75-85% expected to be covered by advance payments and asset-backed financing. Prepayments in the quarter covered over 100% of capex versus 50-60% in Q2, and payback is now 1 year 7 months versus 1 year 10 months. The note gives FY27 revenue guidance as $12-13bn versus $11.7bn consensus in one place and versus $12.0B consensus and roughly in line in another.

SMIC says the AI chip supply chain stays tight through 2027 on data centre and private cloud demand, and memory supply and demand should balance around mid to end 2028. Some equipment orders take over 24 months to deliver.

Telefonica call: analysts pressed on balance sheet, FCF and leverage. BRL has fallen about 8.6% against the euro since the Brazilian election, with 80% of 2027 Brazilian FCF hedged. Investors are asking whether a government sale of its stake before the Spanish election could create overhang. VMO2 leverage is 5.6x in 2026 per GIR, and the Netomnia deal needs CMA approval. The desk's preferred Spain exposure is Zegona.
Other tech items: Travelport denies merger talks with Sabre per Bloomberg, and Meta's Muse agent can now place calls for paid subscribers.

market_movers.rationale: CEO Jensen Huang resigned and Colette Kress is interim CEO. The key uncertainty is whether a new CEO will deploy the balance sheet as aggressively to back the AI ecosystem.
Q3 beat but FY26 revenue guided to the low end of $3.0-3.4B on GPU delays, 2027 capex guided to $40-45B, and the stock carries Nvidia financing-backstop concerns.
Solid quarter with above-consensus guidance. GIR sees share gains and 2027 WFE growth of about 45% versus management's about 30%, implying Street upside.
Beat and raise on networking and opex with strong operating leverage, offset by a product orders miss and decelerating campus and hyperscale orders.
Wise: in-line results plus removal of the Belgium overhang with no admission of wrongdoing, and the desk expects the stock to rise.

sector_views.rationale: GIR sees 2027 WFE growth of about 45% versus about 30% from management and peers, implying upside to Street expectations. The desk calls the AMAT read neutral for the group since most peers have reported.
AMD, AVGO, ANET, CLS and GOOGL gained on the Nvidia CEO news on custom-chip share. SMIC sees AI chip supply staying tight through 2027.
NBIS and CRWV fell on concern over losing Nvidia as the ecosystem's financing backstop, and Nebius delayed FY26 revenue on third-party GPU capacity.

earnings_insights: Cisco F1Q27 (reported 13 Nov): beat and raise on networking and opex. Product orders +21% y/y (+14% ex-webscale AI) missed and decelerated from +35% y/y (+25% ex-webscale) in F4Q26. Campus orders about +15% y/y, a third straight quarter of deceleration.
Applied Materials (reported this week): solid quarter with revenue and margin guidance above expectations. Management guides industry WFE growth of about 30% for 2027, and GIR forecasts about 45%.

CTS Eventim 3Q26 (reported): group revenue EUR 809mn, 2.5% below Vara consensus on weaker Live Entertainment, Ticketing in line. Group adj. EBITDA EUR 134mn in line with consensus, margin 16.5% versus consensus 16.1%. FY26 guidance reiterated.

Nebius Q3 (reported): revenue $981M (+7% vs consensus) and adj. EBITDA $466M (+30% vs consensus). FY26 revenue guidance at the lower end of $3.0-3.4B versus consensus $3.4B. FY27 revenue guidance $12-13bn versus consensus of $11.7bn per one passage, and $12.0B per another. FY27 capex guidance $40-45B versus consensus $28.8B.
Wise (reported): results broadly in line with the Street. Implied H2 net revenue growth about 18% y/y ex-FX versus 22% in H1, versus FY27 guidance of 15-20%. Gross margin 84% in the quarter.
Telefonica (call): analyst focus on balance sheet, FCF and leverage. 80% of Brazilian FCF is hedged in 2027.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Applied Materials management's expectation, in line with peers and constrained by cleanroom additions.
GIR's forecast sits well above management's figure, which GIR says implies upside to Street expectations.

risk_factors: A new Nvidia CEO may lack the willingness or authority to use the balance sheet to back neoclouds and underwrite long-duration demand.
Spying allegations gaining traction could revive US/China regulatory measures such as the MATCH Act.
Nebius guidance shows delays from third-party GPU capacity, and its 2027 capex step-up depends on 75-85% coverage through advance payments and asset-backed financing.
Cisco's growing hyperscale revenue mix may pressure gross margin in F2H27, and orders growth is decelerating.
Telefonica leverage, a possible government stake sale overhang, BRL weakness and VMO2 leverage of 5.6x in 2026 per GIR.
Equipment orders with lead times over 24 months may constrain capital spending, per SMIC.
vol_and_positioning: AMAT: GIR believes investor positioning was very constructive heading into the print given more positive WFE commentary from peers, despite the recent sector-wide selloff.
NVDA opened sharply lower and traded -14.3% at the extreme before closing -4.3%, while QQQ recovered from -1.5% at the open to a modest gain.
geopolitical: Spying allegations tied to the Nvidia CEO resignation could revive broader US/China regulatory measures, including a return of the MATCH Act, negative for ASML and to a lesser extent ASM.
China-exposed names sold off on remote-control rules and potential Megaspeed/Singapore scrutiny.
Brazil election result: BRL has fallen about 8.6% against the euro, with Telefonica hedging 80% of 2027 Brazilian FCF.
Spanish election approaching: investors question whether a sale of the government's Telefonica stake could create overhang.
UK CMA decision on the Netomnia deal is important to VMO2.
